The Regional Land Use and Transportation Plan was adopted by the Milwaukee County Board in May of 1967. The Common Council for the City of Milwaukee adopted it in September 1967 and the community of Oak Creek adopted it on March 6, 1968. The plan was developed cooperatively over a period of three and one-half years by federal, state, regional, county, city and local citizens representing many disciplines and varied interests. Consideration was given to transportation modes, i.e., rail, bus, truck and auto in developing the transportation systems plans. Facility improvements were recommended for highways and buses to accommodate existing and future travel requirements.
This comprehensive planning program takes into account, on a broad scale, the impact upon the environment of all recommended public works improvements. In fact, all regional planning elements are prepared within the framework of a series of objectives, principles, and standards intended not only to provide necessary public facilities to serve existing and future development within the region, but also to insure the preservation and enhancement of the sustaining and underlying natural resource base of the region. (From this plan, figure 12 shows the general land usage of the region as it existed in 1963). If the land use development conforms to the forecasts as expressed in the various local land use plans and corresponding zoning codes, the land use by 1990 will be as shown in figure 6. These land use areas will be served by the region's arterial highway system.
